newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-WILDCARD ORIOLES STUN CLEVELAND FOR 2-0 SERIES LEAD.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-WILDCARD ORIOLES STUN CLEVELAND FOR 2-0 SERIES LEAD.

text.p: The wildcard Baltimore Orioles parlayed two hits, four walks and an error into three eighth-inning runs Wednesday in a 7-4 win over the Cleveland Indians that put the defending American League champions on the brink of elimination.
Catcher Sandy Alomar's throwing error on a double play attempt allowed Cal Ripken to score the eventual winning as Baltimore took a 2-0 lead in the best-of-five divisional playoff series.
"This is the most excited I have been in years," said Ripken. "We can win this but it takes three wins and the last game is always the toughest."

The series shifts to Cleveland Friday, with the Tribe needing a three-game sweep to advance to the league championship series. The Indians are expected to pitch Jack McDowell (13-9) against Mike Mussina (19-10) in Game Three.
Cleveland battled back from a 4-0 deficit with three runs in the sixth, including a two-run homer from Albert Belle, and one run in the top of the eighth to knot the game.

But Baltimore answered in the bottom half. A lead-off walk to Bobby Bonilla and a long double to right centre by Cal Ripken put runners on second and third. Eddie Murray was intentionally walked to load the bases and lefty Paul Assenmacher was summoned to replace reliever Eric Plunk.

Assenmacher got all he could have wished for when BJ Surhoff bounced a comebacker straight to him. The tall lefty tossed home for a force-out at the plate, but Alomar bounced his throw past first baseman Jeff Kent and Ripken dashed home.
The Indians argued that Surhoff had run inside the baseline, interfering with Alomar's line of vision and throwing alley to first, but to no avail.

"Sandy didn't make a good throw, but in our judgment he (Surhoff) was in the base line," Cleveland manager Mike Hargrove said after the game. "The umpires didn't see it that way and said it didn't affect the play."
Pinch hitter Chris Hoiles was then put on intentionally to re-load the bases and this time Brady Anderson delivered with a long sacrifice fly to right that made it 6-4.
Julian Tavarez took over mound duties and promptly walked Todd Zeile to load the bases yet again. Roberto Alomar then completed the scoring with a soft single to right.

Randy Myers worked a 1-2-3 ninth to save the game for hard-throwing reliever Armando Benitez, who had allowed a game-tying sacrifice fly by Julio Franco, but struck out Manny Ramirez and induced Sandy Alomar to pop out to end the Indians' eighth-inning threat.

For the second straight game, the Orioles took the lead in the first inning. After Zeile bounced into a double play, Roberto Alomar and Rafael Palmeiro drew walks off Orel Hershiser before Bonilla grounded a ball through the legs of first baseman Kevin Seitzer, allowing Alomar to score.

The Orioles got to Hershiser again in the fifth when Anderson led off with his second homer of the series. Two outs later, Palmeiro singled, Bonilla walked and Ripken had an RBI single. Murray followed with a double down the left-field line to make it 4-0.

Cleveland rallied in the sixth against starter Scott Erickson. After Jose Vizcaino struck out, Kenny Lofton singled, stole second and third and came home on Seitzer's groundout to second. Jim Thome singled and Albert Belle belted a two-run homer to close the gap to 4-3.

Erickson allowed three runs, six hits and two walks with six strikeouts over 6 2/3 innings. Hershiser, who had a career playof mark of 8-1 with a 1.64 ERA, gave up four runs and seven hits with three walks in five innings.
Anderson, who belted 50 homers during the regular season, said: "It will be much tougher in Cleveland, but they have to take three straight. I like where we are."
